page.layout: Top: two engraved medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend around the rim (left: NINVS, right: SOROASTES). Below them one column of running text, two paragraphs. Page number top left, running head top centre. No margin notes. A fleuron ornament sits below the text.

main_text.p: NINVS, Beli filius, tertius Babyloniorum Rex fuit, anno mundi 1906. ante Christum natum 2056. Regnauit hic 52. annos, omnibus viribus suis sumptis, omnibus bellum inferens, nulli parcés, propter summam regnandi cupiditatem. Primus Babylonicum regnum propagauit, statuam in honore patris Beli erexit, ad quam qui confugerent, omni crimine absol-verentur. Huius exemplo adducti multi, statuas in memoriam patrum erexere. Inde idololatria initium coepit: inde nomina haec, Bel, Baal, Bel-phegor, & Bel-zebub. Videto Hierony.to.6. super Hoseam cap.2. & Bero.lib.5.

ZOROASTES, vt multi autumāt, erat is ipse filius Noë nomine Cham. Fuit hic primus Bactrianorū Rex, primus item artis magicæ inuentor, atque septem artium liberalium, & cursus cœli ac stellarū. Sunt qui memoriæ prodiderint eum simul ac natus est risisse: quod nequaquam fertur bonum omen: cùm nascētes vulgò vagiant. Fuit itaque à Nino victus: fuit quoque ipse Ninus sagitta ictus, quo vulnere periit, hæredem filium relinquens, nomine Niniam. Ninus ciuitatem Niniuen ædificauit, trium dierum circuitum habentem, quam Cyrus Assyriorum Rex euertit. August.lib.de ciuita.Dei 21.cap.14.Euse.Plin. lib.30.cap.7.

page.notes: Medallion legends are engraved in the woodcuts; their letters are read from the rotated rim and marked [?] where uncertain. The fleuron ornament at the foot is not text and is left out. Abbreviations and references are kept as printed; long s is written as plain s.
